messages.subject: Re: Stan models for your book?
parts:
Cool—I’m cc-ing the stan-users list on this one!
A

On Aug 9, 2014, at 8:35 PM, Eric-Jan Wagenmakers <ej.wage...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Bob, (cc Andrew, Martin, Michael)
>
> We would be thrilled to have the examples publicly available in Stan.
> The first few parts of the book are available online at
> bayesmodels.com (we tried to have the publisher put all of it freely
> available online, but they would not budge; someone is bound to just
> scan the book and make it available online though. I am given to
> understand these things happen regularly).
>
> More importantly, *all* of the code from the book is freely available
> online as well (on bayesmodels.com). Martin has been tasked with
> translating the models from JAGS and WinBUGS to Stan, and I was told
> the Stan community has been extremely friendly and helpful.
>
> Martin, feel free to share the code you have so far with Bob and the
> Stan community more generally. It would of course be great if Bob
> could host the code. Michael and I wanted to host the Stan code once
> it was complete, but we can do this earlier as well. Whatever works
> best.
>
> Cheers,
> E.J.
>
> On Fri, Aug 8, 2014 at 7:58 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>> Erik-Jan:
>>
>> People are trying to code the models in your book and
>> asking questions about them on our mailing list.
>>
>> Are the Stan models you guys created for the book available
>> somewhere? I didn't see them on the book's home page.
>>
>> We'd be happy to host them if you want to make them available
>> under an open-source license.
>>
>> - Bob
